description: A correct-but-unusable briefing test. One afternoon, one real pending item, and a lot of near-identical status chatter that invites a briefing to restate every message. Everything a system could say here is true and citable; the failure mode is style — length, hedging, and burying the one actionable line.

ground_truth.notes: This is the bad_style fixture: recall, precision, citation accuracy and hallucination rate can all be perfect while the output is unusable, so none of the numeric metrics catch it. Two named anti-patterns are stored in `unacceptable_briefings`. The first is the transcription failure — every message faithfully restated in speaker-by-speaker order, with the one actionable sentence sitting seventh out of nine and reading like all the others. The second is the hedging failure — so qualified that the user learns nothing and must go read the channel anyway, which defeats the entire product. Both are factually clean. The correct output leads with the signature and the 18:00 cut-off, compresses eight healthy accounts into one clause or drops them, and is short enough to read on a phone. Nine 'nothing needed' style messages against one real item is deliberately the ratio at which a system tuned for completeness produces the first anti-pattern.
